transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 40 mins (approx)
Attendees: Jasmine (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM); Liam (CTO), Asha (Head of ML), Derek (Platform)
Shared artifacts: QBR deck https://app.redwood.ai/decks/QBR-Crimson-05-05, Security pack https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf, Cost spreadsheet (shared in chat)

Summary section (auto):
- Usage up 2.6x in April due to promo; cost spike mainly from high concurrency during checkouts; caching not effective for many short queries.
- Two reliability incidents during peak: swapped model variant fallback initiated late; SE notes kernel OOM on a partic quantized build.
- Customer interested in Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable latency and lower unit costs; also wants VPC/private control plane evaluation for compliance.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jasmine: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll kick off the QBR, got the agenda up there. Priya will go over adoption metrics, Marco will cover reliability and the Dedicated pilot plan.
[00:32] Priya: Hi team, quick context, this is our Q2 check-in for Crimson Retail. We'll run through usage, cost, incidents, and suggested next steps.
[01:05] Liam: Yeah thanks, we had a pretty big promo in April, traffic spiked and we noticed increased latency. Trying to understand where cost is coming from.
[01:28] Marco: Right, so the spike — we looked at token distribution, sequence lengths, and concurrency. Short queries with high concurrency cause suboptimal batching so per-token cost actually goes up.
[01:52] Asha: Just to clarify, these are the user-facing product queries, most under 60 tokens, but 20–30 rps at peak per shard.
[02:15] Marco: Mm-hmm, and that pattern makes continuous batching less effective. Also your prefix cache hits were low because prompts vary a lot, so KV cache doesn't help as much — sometimes shows up as K V cash in the logs, ha.
[02:40] Derek: We also saw a fallback to a smaller model during one of the incidents which increased response variance. That fallback wasn't configured for warm KV state so it added latency.
[03:05] Priya: On costs, we've broken out hosted costs vs projected Dedicated TCO in the deck — short version: Dedicated lowers unit cost at scale but has commit requirements.
[03:30] Liam: What is the SLA gap? During the sale we saw p95 jump above our target of 600ms.
[03:50] Marco: For hosted API we have a 500ms median SLA on standard plans but tails can vary; Dedicated gives you pinned pools and more predictable p95, plus you can request specific autoscale settings.
[04:15] Jasmine: And we can do canary rollouts so you don't flip traffic all at once. We'll show a pilot plan later.
[04:40] Asha: Security is a big one for us — SOC2, SSO, KMS. Do you have the architecture for VPC-private control plane?
[05:05] Priya: Yes, shared in chat — the security pack contains SOC2 attestation, SAML SSO notes, and KMS/HSM integration options. We'll also provide a network diagram for your infra team.
[05:30] Liam: Great. For the reliability incidents, any root cause details? I saw mention of kernel OOMs.
[05:55] Marco: Briefly, one incident looked like kernel selection on a quantized variant hit an OOM for a particular batch shape during the promo spikes. The runtime fell back to a compatible kernel which increased latency; we have a fix in staging to avoid that kernel choice.
[06:20] Asha: Is that the 'quant-2' build you mentioned before?
[06:38] Marco: Yeah, the quant-2 path; we sometimes call it q2 internally, occasionally transcribed as quant too. We're pushing a kernel selection update and a safer fallback policy.
[07:00] Derek: On our side, we can try shifting some offline work to off-peak and also add a small edge cache for very common prompts.
[07:22] Priya: Good idea, Derek. For cost optimization, there are immediate levers: minibatching config, response length caps, and caching common prefixes where applicable.
[07:45] Liam: Curious on the numbers — what's the estimated unit cost improvement on Dedicated?
[08:02] Marco: From our model, about 20–40% reduction in token cost depending on utilization and quantization profile. We'll send a TCO sheet with assumptions.
[08:25] Jasmine: We'll also include expected uplift if you move to q3 quant profile we've seen with similar retailers.
[08:50] Asha: Roadmap-wise, we need a guarantee on data residency and audit logs for compliance audits in Q3. How do you support that?
[09:12] Priya: Private deployment supports customer-managed network and KMS, with audit logs shipped to your logging endpoint; we'll include how to configure retention windows.
[09:35] Liam: Nice. For the pilot, timeline? We're targeting a September enterprise rollout depending on results.
[09:55] Marco: We can aim for a 4–6 week Dedicated pilot: week 1 infra setup, week 2 baseline benchmarks, week 3 tuning, week 4 results + report. If you want faster, we can compress but ups risk.
[10:20] Derek: What infra do we need on our side for VPC peering? Any special ports?
[10:40] Priya: We'll share the network diagram + peering checklist — usually just peering, a small rule set, and optional TLS mutual auth if you require it.
[11:05] Asha: Can we get a test token for the dedicated pilot to run end-to-end load tests?
[11:25] Jasmine: Yes, we'll provision a pilot org token and a reserved pool for the duration.
[11:45] Liam: Any blockers on contract/legal? Procurement usually wants cost certainty.
[12:05] Jasmine: We'll include sample reserved capacity terms in the pricing email. We can do monthly or yearly commits.
[12:30] Marco: Back to reliability, one more note: we recommend enabling prefix caching for the checkout flows where prompts are more stable — that can drop p95 a lot.
[12:50] Derek: We'll identify top 10 prompts to try that.
[13:10] Asha: Are there any notable migration risks from hosted to Dedicated?
[13:30] Marco: The main ones are warm-up time for KV caches and initial throughput tuning. We typically run a canary and a short warm period. Nothing structural.
[13:50] Liam: Regarding observability, can we see token-level cost and per-route latency in the console?
[14:10] Priya: Yes — Redwood Console gives per-route token counts, cost breakdown, and tracing hooks. We'll set up a dashboard for you.
[14:35] Jasmine: Also, we'll enable alerting on p95 breaches for the pilot.
[14:55] Asha: What's the experience for model rollouts? We want safe rollbacks.
[15:15] Marco: We do canaries, A/B, automatic fallback to another variant; rollouts can be configured by route. The console shows rollout status.
[15:35] Derek: Any limitations on function/tool calling or multimodal during Dedicated?
[15:55] Marco: Not really — those are supported but may affect latency depending on kernel selection. We'll capture that in the pilot.
[16:15] Liam: Can you share examples from similar retailers? Any benchmark with similar seq lengths?
[16:35] Marco: Yes, we ran a similar pilot with "Aurora Systems" last quarter; I'll share anonymized results. Expect p50 ~120ms, p95 ~480ms under dedicated pool with similar concurrency.
[16:58] Asha: Great. A couple of asks: 1) security docs and architecture diagram, 2) updated pricing TCO, 3) pilot timeline and test token.
[17:20] Jasmine: We'll action those. Priya will send the security pack, Marco the benchmark plan, and I'll send pricing + contract terms.
[17:40] Priya: I'll also kick off the SOC2 docs share and the network checklist.
[18:02] Liam: On the cost spreadsheet, could you include sensitivity to traffic spikes? We need worst-case monthly bill estimates.
[18:22] Marco: We'll include spike model scenarios; also suggest setting a burst cap or rate limit in the early pilot if you want to protect spend.
[18:40] Derek: Can Redwood provide a simple script to replay a day of traffic against the pilot pool? That would help our perf team.
[19:02] Marco: Yes, we can share a synthetic-replay script, and we'll help run an initial replay if you want.
[19:25] Asha: One last question — do you support HSM-backed KMS?
[19:45] Priya: Yes, HSM integration is available for Private deployments; for hosted we support customer-managed KMS keys via our KMS integration.
[20:05] Liam: Okay sounds good. Any outstanding risks we should note?
[20:25] Jasmine: Short term: kernel OOMs on a particular quant path (being fixed), caching effectiveness low on current prompt diversity, and procurement timeline for Reserved commitments.
[20:45] Liam: Let's capture that.
[21:05] Jasmine: Recap / next steps — action items in chat; Marco will run the benchmark, Priya sends security docs, I'll send pricing. We'll reconvene for pilot review in ~30 days.
[21:35] Derek: Thanks all, appreciate the detail.
[21:50] Asha: Thanks team.
[22:05] Jasmine: End of QBR, folks — we'll follow up via email with links and dates.

(Transcript truncated — remaining conversation was scheduling and short clarifications.)
